audit.why: 52.23% over 1032 games. Maokai's lane damage is low and his only lockdown is a 14s dash-root, so Sett wins every stage until Maokai finishes tank items and converts into peel. EVEN / 6/10 with carry threat 7/10 matches, and the mirror kept the same reading.
audit.corrected: Sett-favoured lane, Maokai-favoured teamfight. Difficulty 6/10 stands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave 'Skill' for levels 4-5, first item and two-plus items. The packet chart gives Sett rows 0-5 and Maokai row 6, the mirror flipped rows 0, 1, 3 and 5 to match it, and this page's own whys say the same ('through levels 4-5 your empowered W shreds his pre-tank frame'; 'at 2+ items Maokai's completed tank build and CC utility outscale your dueling').
audit.why: Packet, mirror and prose all agree; only the three tokens disagreed, and win[6] said Skill while whys[6] named Maokai outright.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Maokai in both layers, ratings re-scaled, and the two full-layer whys sitting on the changed rows rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns called Twisted Advance 'lock-on, undodgeable' with no cooldown and no mention of the part that actually punishes a Sett: he is UNTARGETABLE for the whole dash. A Haymaker or Show Stopper cashed as he casts is spent into nothing.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target.' 14s at rank 1, 525 range. Q is 7s at rank 1 and knocks back. Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 from 1100 range. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1 across 3000 range and creates terrain, which is what cuts a dashless Sett's retreat.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1, untargetable during the dash — wait for him to land, then commit. Bramble Smash 7s, Sapling Toss 18s at 1100 range, Nature's Grasp 130s across 3000.

audit.whatIsWrong: Executioner's Calling is listed with a generic reason and no field explains why Maokai heals so often.
audit.why: Sap Magic heals him on an empowered auto whose cooldown drops every time he casts a spell OR is hit by one — so a long trade where you keep punching him actually accelerates his healing.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds before extended trades: hitting him speeds his own heal up.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Maokai has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours: his damage is still low, so bait Twisted Advance's 14s and cash Haymaker on the pre-tank body while it still hurts.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Twisted Advance (Root) and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two tank items in he stops duelling and becomes peel — W root, saplings, and a 3000-range wall. Take these fights with your team, never alone.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Maokai Twisted Advance: Dashes to a target and roots them — lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (W): 14s at rank 1, 525 range — he is UNTARGETABLE through the dash, so hold your combo until he lands. - Bramble Smash (Q): 7s knockback. - Nature's Grasp (R): 130s at rank 1, 3000 range.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His lock-on root, 14s at rank 1 — he is untargetable mid-dash.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 and reaches 1100 — step off the zone.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Twisted Advance (Root): when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade around Twisted Advance's 14s: down, run the full pattern; up, give nothing. Sap Magic heals him faster the more you hit him, so buy anti-heal.

notes: Restated from the mirror rather than re-derived: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on OPPOSITE sides of Sett, so against a lone Maokai with the wave in front of you it is a slow — this page says 'E-stun' in eight places and none of them carry the condition. The mirror also flagged that the content early/mid/late blocks for this matchup are written in first person elsewhere in the file; the ones on Sett's side read fine. UNVERIFIED and not written: missingInteractions claims The Show Stopper shuts off Twisted Advance via grounding — Riot's R text does not mention grounding, and W's untargetability is the more reliable reason not to commit into it anyway.
